summary: Autoscaler sensitivity to long-lived quiet connections causing reserved capacity lag
description: Issue summary: Customer (AcmeHealth) reports sustained throughput degradation on their dedicated reserved pool beginning 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC. Traffic patterns show many long-lived keepalive connections that send sparse requests (~1 request per 30s) and hold open multiplexed streams for minutes. Autoscaler failed to provision additional GPU slots even as request queue length increased and p99 latency drifted upward. Impact: customer application experienced degraded tail latency and occasional 429s when pinned to reserved pool fallback policies.
impact: Multiple endpoints for AcmeHealth experienced p95/p99 latency increases of 2-3x and intermittent throttling. Customer reported visible errors in production dashboards and product quality degradation for critical wellness workflows. No data loss; throughput reduced by ~40% during the window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant with reserved pool pinned to instance type A100-80GB. 2) Open ~1200 long-lived HTTP/2 keepalive connections that send a request every 20-40 seconds. 3) Mix in short burst requests from separate clients to simulate real traffic. 4) Observe autoscaler attach behavior and GPU slot allocation over 5-15 minute windows. Expected behavior: autoscaler should detect queue growth and provision additional slots within configured cooldown. Observed: autoscaler delayed provisioning and many slots remained reserved but underutilized.
logs:
Relevant traces and logs:
- allocator.log entries 2026-03-10T09:12:03Z: 'heartbeats ok but queue_len=1123, attach_backoff=active'
- autoscaler metrics: scale_decision_delay_ms median=23000, cooldown_remaining_ms=0
- serving-runtime: 'kv-cache pinned, connection_count=1206, avg_inflight_tokens=2'
- network: multiple sockets in CLOSE_WAIT from long-lived client SDKs
- cloud provider metrics: ephemeral GPU attach latency spiked from 120ms -> 850ms between 09:11-09:18 UTC
Dashboards referenced: reserved-pool/AcmeHealth/p99-latency, autoscaler/decision-latency, allocator/slot-utilization.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler heuristics treat long-lived connections with low request frequency as healthy and therefore underreact to queue growth. SRE confirmed autoscaler scoring uses 'active_connection_count' and 'recent_qps' but not 'connection_idle_ratio' leading to misclassification. We observed a noisy neighbor pattern: one internal sidecar process from another tenant produced frequent small keepalives that monopolized session slots, reducing effective slot multiplexing for AcmeHealth. Correlation between sidecar log spike (tenant T-998 logging flood) and the start of degradation is strong (see linked PR and incident).
Additional findings: KV cache residency increased on fewer GPUs causing memory pressure and longer kernel swap times. Autoscaler backoff logic refrains from scaling when it detects transient attach failures; however attach failures here were due to provider-side rate limiting from bursty vm attach operations earlier in the window.

resolution: Mitigation performed: lowered per-tenant autoscaler min_qps_per_connection and temporarily increased reserved pool target for AcmeHealth to absorb backlog. Root cause: autoscaler heuristic did not account for high connection_idle_ratio combined with noisy sidecar from unrelated tenant causing slot hoarding. Permanent actions: (1) Merge autoscaler PR to use connection_idle_ratio in scoring and introduce socket state telemetry (PR linked). (2) Add alert when queue_len > 500 and scale_score < 0.4 to prevent silent underprovisioning. (3) Run capacity hygiene sweep on noisy tenant T-998 and apply rate-limit controls. (4) Update dedicated runbook with diagnostics for long-lived quiet connections. Follow-ups: scheduled postmortem (confluence) and customer remediation guidance for connection reuse and keepalive tuning.
next_steps: 1) Deploy autoscaler scoring changes to staging and run against replayed traffic by 2026-03-16. 2) Create automated regression test that simulates long-lived quiet connections. 3) Share runbook and recommended SDK keepalive settings with AcmeHealth. 4) Monitor reserved pool metrics for 72 hours after full rollout.
notes_for_cs: Customer is sensitive to sustained p99 regressions; they will escalate to account team if recurrence occurs. Provide recommended SDK params: keepalive_interval >= 60s or use shorter connections for low QPS flows; prefer batching. Share ETA for autoscaler fix and confirm temporary config remains until fix is in prod.
